name: Mis

attributes.attribute: an Irish heroine who gave her name to the Slieve Mish mountains
drank her father's blood and went mad after a battle
was healed and tamed by the harper Dubh Rois
became a bard after Dubh Rois fell in battle

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Mis, also called Mish or Miss, was an Irish heroine. The Slieve Mish mountain range in County Kerry bears her name. The place-lore called the Dindshenchas says the mountain was her bride-price. Mis was the daughter of a warrior. After a battle she found her father's bloodied body and, mad with sorrow, drank his blood. The act drove her insane. Mis fled to the mountains and lived by killing animals with her bare hands. A harper named Dubh Rois came and sang, and she crept near to listen. For the first time since her madness she spoke. She asked about his musical instrument, which she remembered from her father's house, and then about his sexual instrument, which she did not remember. Tenderly he showed her both. When Dubh Rois made love to her, Mis lost her wildness and came to love her rescuer. Her recovery was complete, for when Dubh Rois fell in battle she did not go mad again but became a bard to lament him. Scholars note the likeness of this tale to the story of a sovereignty goddess who appears as a hag until kissed and then becomes a beautiful girl. The tale also resembles, with the sexes reversed, the Sumerian taming of the wild man Enkidu by the temple woman Siduri.
objective: Document Mis and the taming of her madness by the harper Dubh Rois.
